# How can a few contact-timing constraints train several biped gaits without joint-by-joint reference motion?

> **Current answer:** Periodic rewards use phase, duty factor, and relative leg phase to compose desired foot-force and swing-velocity timing for standing, walking, running, hopping, and related gaits without copying every joint trajectory. They specify contact rhythm only; phase mismatch, foot slip, impact, torque, and hardware safety still require independent constraints and validation.

## Key terms

- Center of Mass (CoM, 质心)
- Domain Randomization (域随机化)
- Ground Reaction Force (GRF, 地面反作用力)
- Joint Torque (关节力矩)
- Periodic Reward (周期奖励)
- Sim-to-Real (仿真到现实)

## Applicable robots

- Cassie in the paper; other bipeds require new phase, reward, and hardware validation

## Applicable simulators

- MuJoCo/Cassie simulation used by the paper and pinned APEX implementation

## Controllers and methods

- Phase-conditioned biped locomotion policy
- Periodic-reward reinforcement learning

## Applicable environments

- Periodic standing, walking, running, hopping, and gait-transition tasks

## Assumptions

- A periodic phase variable and desired contact rhythm are meaningful for the target gait.
- Torque, impact, posture, and slip are checked outside the contact clock.

## Result

- Periodic rewards use phase, duty factor, and relative leg phase to compose desired foot-force and swing-velocity timing for standing, walking, running, hopping, and related gaits without copying every joint trajectory. They specify contact rhythm only; phase mismatch, foot slip, impact, torque, and hardware safety still require independent constraints and validation.

## Limitations

- A periodic phase variable and desired contact rhythm are meaningful for the target gait.
- Torque, impact, posture, and slip are checked outside the contact clock.
